sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Because of the limitations of geotechnical explorations and geologic interpretations, there is always the possibility that significant deviations from anticipated subsurface conditions might be encountered. In addition, construction operations can change the behavior of in-place soils, as well as the foundation support and stability of nearby facilities. Therefore, observations by an experienced geotechnical engineer during construction are recommended to identify additional concerns in the field and to provide adjustments to the design when necessary. The contracting agency's construction personnel normally provide inspection and monitoring. The geotechnical report should discuss anticipated ground conditions at the footing bearing level and explain how to identify expected ground conditions to the inspection staff.
key_points: Subsurface conditions may deviate significantly from geotechnical exploration interpretations
Construction operations can change in-place soil behavior and stability of nearby facilities
Experienced geotechnical engineer observation during construction is recommended
Geotechnical report should describe anticipated conditions at footing bearing level
Inspection staff should know how to identify expected ground conditions and contact designers
Geotechnical staff may need to make site visits for questionable conditions or specialized instrumentation
sections.applicability: General guidance on the need for geotechnical inspection and monitoring during shallow foundation construction.

sections.title: Inspection
sections.body: Inspection of foundation construction is only as good as the qualifications and experience of the inspector. A competent inspector follows systematic inspection and documentation procedures and communicates issues with the foundation designer. Foundations are designed to: perform within settlement tolerances, maintain adequate safety margin against bearing capacity failure, provide frictional resistance against sliding, provide resistance against lateral earth pressures, and provide sufficient support to prevent slope instability. Accepting materials or procedures different from those specified could compromise the design intent and potentially lead to distress or failure. Exceeding a criterion (e.g., over-compaction behind an abutment wall) can increase stresses on the foundation element. Groundwater impacts can be serious: dewatering with sumps may compromise temporary sloped excavation stability, while dewatering wells can induce consolidation settlement in clay profiles. Improper construction methods can lead to foundation and slope failures. The inspector should regularly observe foundation and slope conditions for potential weaknesses. Surface water and precipitation can deteriorate moisture-sensitive bearing materials. Footing excavation bottoms can be probed with rods for bearing resistance confirmation, or tested with CPT and nuclear densometers.
key_points: Inspector qualifications and experience are critical to construction quality
Foundations must satisfy: settlement, bearing capacity, sliding, lateral earth pressure, and slope stability criteria
Accepting non-specified materials or procedures can compromise design intent
Over-compaction behind abutment walls can increase stresses on foundation elements
Dewatering with sumps may compromise temporary sloped excavation stability
Dewatering wells can induce consolidation settlement in clay profiles
Inspector should regularly observe foundation and slope conditions for potential weaknesses
Footing excavation bottoms can be probed with rods or tested with CPT and nuclear densometers
Moisture-sensitive bearing materials must be protected from surface water and precipitation
Test pit excavation into bearing stratum should be avoided due to difficulty compacting backfill
sections.applicability: Inspection procedures and critical observations during shallow foundation construction.

sections.title: Materials
sections.body: Material inspection for shallow foundation construction includes verifying line, grade and bearing elevation; checking the in-place bearing stratum; and ensuring structural fill materials meet specifications.
key_points: Material inspection covers line/grade, bearing stratum verification, and fill material compliance
Three key inspection areas: location/elevation, bearing stratum condition, structural fill quality
sections.applicability: Overview of material inspection requirements for shallow foundation construction.

sections.title: Line, Grade and Bearing Elevation
sections.body: The agency inspector should confirm that surveyed locations and elevations of footing elements conform to the plans and shop drawings. Where foundation elevations and location vary from those specified, the actual dimensions should be documented and then checked with the designer for concurrence.
key_points: Confirm surveyed footing locations and elevations match plans and shop drawings
Document and check with designer any deviations from specified elevations or locations
sections.applicability: Verifying footing location and elevation during construction.

sections.title: Bearing Stratum
sections.body: The in-place bearing stratum of soil or rock should be checked to verify the in situ condition and the degree of improvement achieved by the contractor's preparation approach. Some soil types can become remolded and weakened from disturbance. If conditions deviate from those anticipated in the geotechnical report and/or plans, the geotechnical engineer should be consulted to determine if additional measures are necessary.
key_points: Verify in situ condition of bearing stratum and effectiveness of contractor's preparation
Some soils can be remolded and weakened by construction disturbance
Consult geotechnical engineer if conditions deviate from those anticipated in the geotechnical report
sections.applicability: Verifying bearing stratum conditions during shallow foundation construction.

sections.title: Structural Fill Materials
sections.body: Fill requirements should be strictly adhered to because the fill must perform within expected limits for strength (bearing capacity) and, more importantly, within tolerance for differential settlement. Sometimes the construction area is small (e.g., abutment and wingwall backfill), which may necessitate smaller compaction equipment. Testing should verify: material gradation and durability at sufficient frequency, specified compaction level in accordance with standard operating procedures and at recommended test intervals, and surcharge fill unit weight where pre-loading is required.
key_points: Fill requirements must be strictly followed for bearing capacity and differential settlement performance
Small construction areas (abutment/wingwall backfill) may require smaller compaction equipment
Test material gradation and durability at sufficient frequency
Verify compaction meets specification per standard procedures and recommended test intervals
Verify surcharge fill unit weight meets design assumptions where pre-loading is specified
sections.applicability: Inspecting and verifying structural fill materials during shallow foundation construction.

sections.title: Monitoring
sections.body: When monitoring construction of structural fills that will support shallow foundations, particular attention should be paid to material gradation and durability testing, specified compaction levels, and surcharge fill unit weight verification. Foundation elevations should be checked before and after structural load application to serve as a baseline for long-term bridge monitoring. Additional survey measurements can confirm satisfactory performance or identify potentially harmful settlements. It may be important to check completion of fill settlements before foundation construction if soft compressible soils exist below. Lateral displacement potential can be greater than vertical movements; monitoring may include survey coordinates and instrumentation. Monitoring may also be necessary to evaluate impacts on neighboring ground and facilities using survey tag lines, monitoring hubs, telltales, inclinometers, extensometers, strain gages, and tiltmeters. Pre-existing condition surveys of neighboring structures are valuable, particularly in congested urban areas. The instrumentation program should be developed considering anticipated performance, risks, and potential consequences, with timely data interpretation for corrective measures.
key_points: Check foundation elevations before and after structural load application for long-term monitoring baseline
Survey measurements confirm performance or identify potentially harmful settlements
Check completion of fill settlements before foundation construction over soft compressible soils
Lateral displacement potential can exceed vertical movements
Monitoring instruments: survey tag lines, hubs, telltales, inclinometers, extensometers, strain gages, tiltmeters
Pre-existing condition surveys of neighboring structures are valuable in congested urban areas
Instrumentation program should consider anticipated performance, risks, and consequences
Timely data interpretation is key to taking corrective measures when needed
sections.applicability: Monitoring construction and long-term performance of shallow foundations and structural fills.
